title: Company-wide policies and processes (access, change management, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates)
author: Amira Patel
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and core operational processes for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and internal templates. It is intended for all employees, managers, and team leads. Where specific teams (security, finance, legal, IT) have owner-level responsibilities those are called out.

Primary objectives:
- Provide a single reference for commonly used company policies and operational procedures.
- Ensure consistent approvals, auditability, and compliance with internal SLAs.
- Reduce ambiguity for new hires and cross-functional partners.

1) Access & Permissions

Scope: corporate systems (SSO/Identity Provider), internal services (databases, dashboards), cloud accounts, and vendor consoles.

Policy summary:
- Principle of least privilege: users receive minimum access required for their role.
- Role-based access: teams should use predefined roles where available (e.g., eng-readonly, eng-deployer, finance-approver).
- Temporary elevated access: time-limited grants (max 7 days for routine tasks) via Access Request workflow.
- Quarterly access reviews: managers and application owners must review membership lists and role mappings.

Access request process (standard):
1. Employee submits an Access Request via the internal Access Portal (link: /tools/access-portal). Include purpose, duration, and approver.
2. Manager approves or rejects within 48 hours. If approver is unavailable escalate to manager-on-call.
3. System owner (application owner) performs technical approval within 72 hours.
4. Access is provisioned by IT/Identity team and tagged with ticket ID.
5. All temporary grants auto-expire; requestor receives a reminder 2 days before expiry.

Emergency access (break-glass):
- Use the emergency access process documented in /oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks. Break-glass requires immediate post-facto justification and a security review within 3 business days.

Access review cadence and owners:
| Area | Owner | Review Frequency | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| SSO / IAM roles | IT Identity | Quarterly | Exported reports retained 1 year |
| Databases (prod) | Data Platform | Monthly | Include active DB credentials & service accounts |
| Cloud accounts | Cloud Ops | Quarterly | Cross-check billing owners |

2) Change Management

Goal: Minimize operational risk from configuration, infra, and software changes while enabling fast iteration. Applies to: production and production-adjacent systems (datastores, control plane, runtime services).

Change categories:
- Standard change: low risk, repeatable (e.g., minor config tweak). Pre-approved and logged.
- Normal change: requires change request (CR), impact assessment, and approval by change advisory board (CAB).
- Emergency change: must be followed by an emergency change record and post-implementation review.

Normal change process:
1. Initiate CR in the Change Management system with owner, rollback plan, and test plan.
2. Risk assessment by service owner. If high-risk, schedule CAB review.
3. Approvals: service owner (required), security (if affects auth/data), SRE (if affects availability).
4. Implement during approved change window.
5. Post-change verification and update runbooks.

Change windows and SLAs:
- Standard maintenance window: Sat 02:00–06:00 UTC. Teams may request exceptions.
- CR approval SLA: 72 hours for normal changes. Emergency changes: 4-hour response target.

Rollback & testing requirements:
- Every CR must include a documented rollback plan and success/failure criteria.
- Run automated preflight tests for any change impacting runtime or data paths.

3) Data Management

Principles: classify, protect, minimize retention, and enable responsible access.

Data classification tiers:
- Public: safe for public disclosure (docs, marketing materials).
- Internal: company-internal (non-sensitive).
- Confidential: internal + contractual restrictions (customer data, contracts).
- Restricted: regulated data (PII, billing, health-related) requiring elevated controls.

Data handling requirements:
- Encryption: data at rest and in transit must use approved encryption (AES-256 at rest, TLS1.2+ in transit).
- Access controls: RBAC + just-in-time access; all privileged actions logged.
- Data minimization: only store fields required for product function or compliance.
- Retention: default retention periods by type (see table).

Retention & backup table:
| Data type | Typical retention | Owner | Backup frequency |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| Audit logs | 1 year | Security | Daily |
| Production DB backups | 90 days | Data Platform | Daily |
| Customer PII | 7 years (or contract) | Legal/Compliance | Snapshot daily |
| Analytics events | 365 days | Product Analytics | Hourly aggregation |

Data access request process:
- Requests for Confidential/Restricted data must route through Data Access Request (DAR) workflow. Include justification, retention plan, and approver (data owner). Security will perform a privacy impact assessment for Restricted data.

Data incidents and breach notification:
- Follow the Security incident response playbook. Notify Legal & Security within 1 hour of detection. Customer-impacting incidents trigger customer notification timelines per contracts.

4) Procurement & Expenses

Policy highlights:
- All purchases > $5,000 require a Purchase Order (PO) and Procurement team approval.
- Recurring SaaS contracts > $1,000/month require Procurement & Finance review plus Legal sign-off if contract term > 12 months.
- Corporate card usage: follow the expenses policy; personal charges are prohibited.

Procurement process (high level):
1. Requestor fills out Purchase Request form (template included below).
2. Manager approves based on budget and need.
3. Procurement evaluates vendor terms, obtains at least two quotes for purchases > $15,000.
4. Finance verifies budget and issues PO.
5. Vendor onboarding (see Vendor Management) and payment terms agreed.

Expense reimbursement rules:
- Submit receipts within 30 days. Reimbursements processed weekly. Approver is direct manager; Finance performs periodic audits.

Purchase Request template (use copy in internal templates):
- Requestor name:
- Team & cost center:
- Description of goods/services:
- Estimated cost:
- Vendor name & contact:
- Business justification and benefits:
- Requested delivery date:
- Approval chain (manager, procurement, finance)

5) Vendor Management

Purpose: ensure vendors meet Redwood security, privacy, and contractual standards. Applies when vendors handle company data, run code in our environment, or integrate with customer data.

Vendor onboarding checklist:
1. Vendor intake form and initial risk questionnaire.
2. Legal reviews T&Cs and negotiates Data Processing Agreement (DPA) if needed.
3. Security completes a vendor security assessment (self-assessment or 3rd party attestation like SOC2).
4. Procurement agrees pricing and SLA.
5. Technical integration plan and access scope documented.

Vendor risk tiers & controls:
- Low: marketing tools, non-sensitive SaaS. Standard contract and annual review.
- Medium: vendors with access to internal systems or aggregated data. Require DPA and quarterly review.
- High: vendors processing customer data or running code in infra. Require DPA, SOC2/ISO certification, periodic security testing, and executive sponsor approval.

Offboarding: revoke credentials, remove service accounts, and ensure data deletion per contract. Verify with vendor within 30 days and retain record in vendor registry.

6) Travel & Expense Policy (summary)

Booking and approvals:
- All work travel must be pre-approved by manager. International travel requires travel risk review for high-risk countries (Travel team/People Ops).

Allowable expenses & per diems:
- Meals: actuals up to $75/day domestic, $125/day international unless otherwise approved.
- Hotels: up to $250/night in major metros; exceptions require manager pre-approval.
- Airfare: economy or 'premium economy' only with manager approval for flights > 6 hours.

Expense submission:
1. Submit itemized receipts via Expense tool within 14 days of trip end.
2. Attach conference agenda (if applicable) and business justification.
3. Manager approves; Finance processes reimbursement in the next payroll cycle.

Safety & insurance:
- Company travel insurance is active for approved business trips. Report incidents to People Ops and Security immediately.

7) Internal Templates & Quick Links

Common templates (copyable from the Templates library):
- Purchase Request (Procurement)
- Vendor Intake & Risk Questionnaire
- Access Request form
- Change Request (normal/emergency)
- Data Access Request (DAR)
- Travel Approval & Expense form

Quick links:
- Access Portal: /tools/access-portal
- Change Management: /tools/change-management
- Procurement Catalog: /tools/procurement-catalog
- Vendor Registry: /tools/vendor-registry
- Expense Tool: /tools/expenses
- Templates library: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates

Governance, exceptions & escalation
- Exceptions to any policy must be requested via the Exceptions Request form and approved by the owning team (People Ops for HR-related policies, Security for access/data, Finance for procurement/expenses). Exceptions should include risk mitigation and a sunset date.
- Escalation matrix:
1. Manager
2. Team lead / service owner
3. Owning team (People Ops / Security / Finance / Procurement)
4. CTO / CFO for unresolved or strategic exceptions

Audit & compliance
- Teams must be prepared to provide evidence of approvals, access logs, and retention settings for internal or external audits. Security and Finance will run annual compliance audits.

Appendix: Example change request checklist
1. CR title and ID
2. Service owner and contact
3. Impacted systems and rollback plan
4. Testing checklist (pre/post)
5. Monitoring/alerting runbook updates
6. Stakeholder notification list

End of document.
